pictures.scene: Frederic Edwin Church, The Heart of the Andes — the whole world opening away in light from the flowers at your feet to the snow peak, bless the LORD O my soul, O LORD my God You are very great
pictures.name: pd_church_ziel

pictures.scene: Giovanni Bellini, The Transfiguration — Christ standing changed on the hill with the light coming off Him, You are clothed with splendor and majesty, He wraps Himself in light as with a garment
pictures.name: pd_bellini_luister

pictures.scene: Jacob van Ruisdael, Wheat Fields — the enormous sky pitched over the corn like a tent, He stretches out the heavens like a tent, laying the beams of His chambers
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_tent

pictures.scene: Raphael, The Vision of Ezekiel — God borne up through the cloud on the living creatures, in the waters above, making the clouds His chariot
pictures.name: pd_rafael_wagen

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Archangel Raphael Leaving Tobias' Family — the angel going up into the air on great wings while the family falls back, walking on the wings of the wind, He makes the winds His messengers
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_wind

pictures.scene: Dieric Bouts the Elder, Moses and the Burning Bush — the bush standing in flame and not burning up while Moses takes off his shoes, flames of fire His servants, He set the earth on its foundations
pictures.name: pd_bouts_vuur

pictures.scene: Claude-Joseph Vernet, A Shipwreck in Stormy Seas — the sea coming over everything under a black sky, never to be moved, You covered it with the deep like a garment
pictures.name: pd_vernet_diep

pictures.scene: Albert Bierstadt, A Storm in the Rocky Mountains — the storm cloud piled higher than the peaks and the water lying below, the waters stood above the mountains, at Your rebuke the waters fled
pictures.name: pd_bierstadt_bergen

pictures.scene: Thomas Moran, The Chasm of the Colorado — the gorge cut down through the rock under a breaking storm, at the sound of Your thunder they hurried away, the mountains rose and the valleys sank
pictures.name: pd_moran_donder

pictures.scene: Aelbert Cuyp, The Maas at Dordrecht — the wide river lying still against its own shore in golden light, to the place You assigned for them, You set a boundary they cannot cross
pictures.name: pd_cuyp_grens

pictures.scene: Allaert van Everdingen, Landscape with a Waterfall — the spring water coming down over the rocks out of the high ground, that they may never again cover the earth, He sends forth springs in the valleys

pictures.scene: Paulus Potter, Cows near a Farm — the cattle standing at the water's edge in the heat of the day, they flow between the mountains, they give drink to every beast of the field
pictures.name: pd_potter_drenken

pictures.scene: Melchior d'Hondecoeter, Water Birds — ducks and herons and every kind of bird gathered at the pool, the wild donkeys quench their thirst, the birds of the air nest beside the springs
pictures.name: pd_hondecoeter_vogels

pictures.scene: Asher Brown Durand, In the Woods — the green shade of the deep forest with the stream running under the fallen trunks, they sing among the branches, He waters the mountains from His chambers
pictures.name: pd_durand_takken

pictures.scene: Charles-Émile Jacque, Sheep at Pasture — the flock spread out over good grass with the shepherd behind them, the earth is satisfied by the fruit of His works, He makes the grass grow for the livestock
pictures.name: pd_jacque_gras

pictures.scene: Jules Breton, The Gleaners — the women bent over the cut field gathering what the harvest left, and provides crops for man to cultivate, bringing forth food from the earth
pictures.name: pd_breton_gewas

pictures.scene: Léon Augustin Lhermitte, The Grape Harvest — the pickers carrying in the full baskets from the vines, wine that gladdens the heart of man
pictures.name: pd_lhermitte_wijn

pictures.scene: Louis Le Nain, A Peasant Family — the poor family gathered around the loaf and the cup with the firelight on their faces, oil that makes his face to shine, and bread that sustains his heart
pictures.name: pd_lenain_brood

pictures.scene: Camille Corot, Forest of Fontainebleau — the great old trees standing full and heavy over the clearing, the trees of the LORD have their fill, the cedars of Lebanon that He planted
pictures.name: pd_corot_bomen

pictures.scene: Vincent van Gogh, Cypresses — the dark trees turning like flame up into the summer sky, where the birds build their nests, the stork makes her home in the cypresses
pictures.name: pd_gogh_cipres

pictures.scene: Edwin Landseer, The Monarch of the Glen — the stag standing on the high ground above the mist with his head up, the high mountains are for the wild goats, the cliffs a refuge for the rock badgers
pictures.name: pd_landseer_geiten

pictures.scene: Aert van der Neer, Moonlit Landscape with a Bridge — the moon standing over the river and the last light gone out of the sky, He made the moon to mark the seasons, the sun knows when to set
pictures.name: pd_neer_maan

pictures.scene: Rosa Bonheur, Portrait of a Lion — the lion's head out of the dark with his eyes open and watching, You bring darkness and it becomes night, when all the beasts of the forest prowl
pictures.name: pd_bonheur_leeuw

pictures.scene: George Inness, Sunrise — the sun coming up through the trees and burning the mist off the field, and seek their food from God, the sun rises and they withdraw
pictures.name: pd_inness_zon

pictures.scene: Ilya Repin, Barge Haulers on the Volga — the men leaning into the harness dragging the barge up the river, they lie down in their dens, man goes forth to his work
pictures.name: pd_repin_werk

pictures.scene: Charles-François Daubigny, Sunset at Villerville — the day going down red over the water and the shore, and to his labor until evening, how many are Your works O LORD
pictures.name: pd_daubigny_avond

pictures.scene: Jan Brueghel the Younger, Paradise Landscape with Animals — every creature of the earth gathered together in one green place, in wisdom You have made them all, the earth is full of Your creatures
pictures.name: pd_brueghel_schepsel

pictures.scene: Hendrik Willem Mesdag, Calm Sea — the open water running out flat and grey to the edge of the sky, here is the sea vast and wide, teeming with creatures beyond number
pictures.name: pd_mesdag_zee

pictures.scene: J. M. W. Turner, The Fighting Téméraire — the old ship brought up the river through the burning evening, living things both great and small, there the ships pass
pictures.name: pd_turner_schepen

pictures.scene: Hendrick van Anthonissen, View of Scheveningen Sands — the great whale lying on the beach with the townsfolk come out to look at it, and Leviathan which You formed to frolic there, all creatures look to You
pictures.name: pd_anthonissen_leviathan

pictures.scene: Ambrosius Francken I, The Multiplication of the Loaves and Fishes — the baskets carried out through the crowd until everyone has enough, to give them their food in due season, when You give it to them
pictures.name: pd_francken_voedsel

pictures.scene: Pieter Aertsen, Market Woman at a Vegetable Stand — the stall heaped with everything the ground has given, they gather it up, when You open Your hand
pictures.name: pd_aertsen_verzamelen

pictures.scene: Fritz von Uhde, Grace at Table — the poor family with their hands folded over the bread before they eat, they are satisfied with good things, when You hide Your face
pictures.name: pd_uhde_verzadigd

pictures.scene: Andrea Mantegna, The Crucifixion — the sky gone hard over Golgotha and the watchers standing stricken at the foot of the cross, they are terrified, when You take away their breath
pictures.name: pd_mantegna_ontsteld

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Entombment of Christ — the dead body let down out of their hands toward the stone, they die and return to dust, when You send Your Spirit
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_stof

pictures.scene: Thomas Cole, The Garden of Eden — the first world standing new and unspoiled with the water falling through it, they are created, and You renew
pictures.name: pd_cole_geschapen

pictures.scene: Vincent van Gogh, Almond Blossom — the bare branches breaking out into white flower against the blue, the face of the earth, may the glory of the LORD endure forever
pictures.name: pd_gogh_aanschijn

pictures.scene: John Frederick Kensett, Lake George — the still lake lying between the wooded headlands with the far peaks beyond, may the LORD rejoice in His works, He looks on the earth
pictures.name: pd_kensett_verheugt

pictures.scene: Johan Christian Dahl, An Eruption of Vesuvius — the lava running down the mountain and the smoke going up off the red crater, and it trembles, He touches the mountains
pictures.name: pd_dahl_beeft

pictures.scene: Orazio Gentileschi, Saint Cecilia and an Angel — the saint with her hands on the organ keys and the angel holding the music open for her, and they smolder, I will sing to the LORD all my life
pictures.name: pd_gentileschi_zingen

pictures.scene: Gerrit Dou, An Old Woman Reading the Bible — the old woman bent close over the great open book with her hands on the page, I will sing praise to my God while I have my being, may my meditation be pleasing to Him
pictures.name: pd_dou_overdenking

pictures.scene: Mariotto Albertinelli, The Visitation — Mary and Elizabeth meeting under the arch and holding one another as the Magnificat begins, for I rejoice in the LORD, may sinners vanish from the earth
pictures.name: pd_albertinelli_verblijd

pictures.scene: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, The Immaculate Conception — the Virgin carried up in golden light with her hands joined and her eyes lifted, and the wicked be no more, bless the LORD O my soul
pictures.name: pd_murillo_zegen

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, The Coronation of the Virgin — the whole court of heaven with the trumpets and the lutes and the saints kneeling before the throne, Hallelujah
pictures.name: pd_angelico_halleluja

lines.text: Bless the LORD, O my soul!
O LORD my God, You are very great;
You are clothed with splendor and majesty.
He wraps Himself in light as with a garment;
He stretches out the heavens like a tent,
laying the beams of His chambers
in the waters above,
making the clouds His chariot,
walking on the wings of the wind.
He makes the winds His messengers,
flames of fire His servants.
He set the earth on its foundations,
never to be moved.
You covered it with the deep like a garment;
the waters stood above the mountains.
At Your rebuke the waters fled;
at the sound of Your thunder they hurried away—
the mountains rose and the valleys sank
to the place You assigned for them—
You set a boundary they cannot cross,
that they may never again cover the earth.
He sends forth springs in the valleys;
they flow between the mountains.
They give drink to every beast of the field;
the wild donkeys quench their thirst.
The birds of the air nest beside the springs;
they sing among the branches.
He waters the mountains from His chambers;
the earth is satisfied by the fruit of His works.
He makes the grass grow for the livestock
and provides crops for man to cultivate,
bringing forth food from the earth:
wine that gladdens the heart of man,
oil that makes his face to shine,
and bread that sustains his heart.
The trees of the LORD have their fill,
the cedars of Lebanon that He planted,
where the birds build their nests;
the stork makes her home in the cypresses.
The high mountains are for the wild goats,
the cliffs a refuge for the rock badgers.
He made the moon to mark the seasons;
the sun knows when to set.
You bring darkness, and it becomes night,
when all the beasts of the forest prowl.
The young lions roar for their prey
and seek their food from God.
The sun rises, and they withdraw;
they lie down in their dens.
Man goes forth to his work
and to his labor until evening.
How many are Your works, O LORD!
In wisdom You have made them all;
the earth is full of Your creatures.
Here is the sea, vast and wide,
teeming with creatures beyond number,
living things both great and small.
There the ships pass,
and Leviathan, which You formed to frolic there.
All creatures look to You
to give them their food in due season.
When You give it to them,
they gather it up;
when You open Your hand,
they are satisfied with good things.
When You hide Your face,
they are terrified;
when You take away their breath,
they die and return to dust.
When You send Your Spirit,
they are created,
and You renew
the face of the earth.
May the glory of the LORD endure forever;
may the LORD rejoice in His works.
He looks on the earth,
and it trembles;
He touches the mountains,
and they smolder.
I will sing to the LORD all my life;
I will sing praise to my God while I have my being.
May my meditation be pleasing to Him,
for I rejoice in the LORD.
May sinners vanish from the earth
and the wicked be no more.
Bless the LORD, O my soul.
Hallelujah!
